the sol-gel process allows one to prepare doped matrices with high optical quality, that the chemistry of the organic molecules in the sol-gel matrices is influenced by the surface chemistry of the silica particles formed early in gel formation, and that the luminescence of the organic dyes in these matrices is influenced by changes in the hydrophobic character of the particles.
the sol-gel process allows one to prepare transparent oxide matrices damped with organic dyes and that the interactions between the dye and the oxide matrix depend on the chemistry of both species.

the luminescence of pyrenine-doped gels changes during gelation, indicating a strong decrease in their hydrophilic character, while the initial pH of rhodamine-B and 6G-silica gels has a strong effect on the dye chemistry.
